name: Field
summary: Wires one label, one description and one error message to one form control, and passes the invalid, disabled, read only and required state to it.
useWhen: Any form control that needs a visible label
A control with a hint that helps fill it, or an error that says how to fix the value
A settings row with the label at the start and the control at the end (orientation horizontal)
avoidWhen: A search box in a toolbar whose purpose is plain from an icon and an aria-label
A group of checkboxes or radios that shares one question
Read only text that is not a control

orientation.description: vertical: label above the control. horizontal: label at the start of the control's line.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. When not passed, the field is invalid while an error message shows. false hides the error.

readOnly.description: Passed to the control. Still focusable and readable.

required.description: Shows the required mark and sets aria-required on the control.

label.description: One line API: renders FieldLabel, the system Label with data-part label.

error.description: One line API: renders the system FieldError with data-part error.

a11y.role: none on the root. The label is a native label bound to the control with for and id.
a11y.focus: The root is never focusable. Clicking the label focuses the control.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control. The field adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The description, then the error, are read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The error is not a live region and never role alert, so an error that is there when the page loads does not interrupt.
notes: The required mark is an asterisk glyph, so it does not rely on color, and it is aria-hidden. The control carries aria-required, not the native required attribute, so the browser shows no validation bubble.
The error starts with a danger icon, so it does not rely on color.
Controls read the wiring with useFieldControl(): id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly. A value the control passes itself wins.
A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first invalid control.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.
The label part is a Label root (data-ds label) and the error part a FieldError root (data-ds field-error). The required mark and the error icon belong to those components' anatomy.

en.label: A noun in sentence case that names the value: Email, Board name. No colon, no question.
en.description: One sentence that helps fill the field or says where the value shows. Not a repeat of the label.
en.error: Says what to do, in plain words: Add the part after the @. Never only Invalid or Required.
en.placeholder: Never the label. An example value at most: For example, spring launch.
en.required: Mark required fields with * and say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

ar.label: اسم بصيغة المصدر أو الاسم، بدون تشكيل: البريد الإلكتروني، اسم اللوحة
ar.description: جملة وحدة توضح وش يكتب أو وين تظهر القيمة
ar.error: يقول وش يسوي عشان يصلحها: البريد ناقص، اكتبه كامل. مو بس غلط
ar.placeholder: ما يكون بديل عن العنوان. مثال على القيمة بس
ar.latin: النص اللاتيني داخل العربي يمر عبر Bidi
ar.required: سطر واحد فوق النموذج: الحقول اللي عليها * مطلوبة

react.behavior: hand built context, Label and FieldError as parts

styles.studio: Lays out the Label, the control, a muted description and the FieldError
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder used as the label
mistakes.right: A FieldLabel above the control, and an example value in the placeholder at most

mistakes.wrong: An error that only says Invalid email
mistakes.right: An error that says how to fix it: Add the part after the @, for example name@example.com

mistakes.wrong: role alert on an inline error that is there when the page loads
mistakes.right: FieldError, read through aria-describedby when focus lands on the control

mistakes.wrong: A red asterisk as the only sign of a required field
mistakes.right: required on Field: an aria-hidden asterisk glyph plus aria-required on the control

mistakes.wrong: A label with an id written by hand and a control with a different id
mistakes.right: Field gives both ids. A control id of its own is picked up by the label.
